teams.synopsis: Feared once again — Slansky opened with a league-high 152.76 points.
teams.blurb: A talented manager that has a stellar history of being 16-9 in the regular season for the past two fantasy years. Slansky should be feared by all again this year — putting up the most points in Week 1, 152.76.

teams.synopsis: A middle-round steal in AJ Dillon has the Tiger King off to a 1-0 start.
teams.blurb: Being placed as high as number 2 might come as a shock to some, but he has a knack for proving opposing managers wrong with his ability to find talent in the middle rounds of the draft. That ability allowed him to draft AJ Dillon this year, putting up 20 points this previous week for the Tiger King — granting him status of being 1-0 and the third highest league scorer in Week 1.

teams.synopsis: The reigning champ looks nearly flawless again, Dak injury and all.
teams.blurb: The reigning champ is picking up right where he left off — could we see the first repeat winner in the PFFL? Krispy Kareems may not have a weakness in his lineup, aside from his flex and potentially his TE due to Dak being sidelined 8 weeks, but having the best QB partnered with a top-5 wide receiver makes this team a matchup nightmare.

teams.synopsis: Lost the week but not the promise — a top TE and A Rob upside keep the outlook sky-high.
teams.blurb: I can already hear it: “How can someone who lost Week 1 be higher than people who won the week, especially his opponent?” All I can say is that this team has a lot of promise. There are a few question marks with this receiver corps, but if A Rob can become the player that Broncos Country drafted him to be, then the sky's the limit for this team. Also, having the non-debatable top TE gives you a significant advantage among other fantasy managers.

teams.synopsis: Mount Rushmore talk aside, Breece's Pieces needs King Henry to fix an 8-17 history.
teams.blurb: When you talk about fantasy sports and the Mount Rushmore of managers, you must say Ryan McQuaid, right? Well, what if we narrowed it down to the PFFL Mount Rushmore — that changes a few things. Breece's Pieces has had a shaky career in the PFFL with an overall regular season record of 8-17, but hopefully this year is different with King Henry at the helm.

teams.synopsis: Boom-or-bust incarnate — league-high booms and busts both, but a Week 1 win regardless.
teams.blurb: Could this be the year that Nicholas Cruz doesn't get unlucky and avoids injuries? He's been plagued with torn ACLs and hamstring issues his entire fantasy career, but he looks to shock the world with a win in Week 1 and the WR1 on his team. In Week 1, this team had a league-high amount of players boom (4 players), while also having a league-high amount of players bust (6 players) — leading to the evaluation that this team is in for many ups and many downs this year.

teams.synopsis: Four quarterbacks looked excessive until Dak went down for 8 weeks — foresight paying off early.
teams.blurb: Questioned on draft night for his choice to take 4 quarterbacks, but it looks like it was needed because of the loss of Dak for the next 8 weeks. The longest-tenured team name, San Giacomos Frannys Fanny, is back this season for his shot at being known as one of the best. The win in Week 1 is impressive with Dak getting injured, but the team finished with less points than the league's Points For Average (115.59). Will his luck continue in Week 2, or will he have to trade for a much-needed WR2?

teams.synopsis: A deep 2020 run, a last-place 2021 — and a quietly loaded roster building a case for a return trip.
teams.blurb: The back end of our rankings starts off with Chicago We Got Um, who looks to finally make the finals this year after a deep playoff run in 2020 and a last-place finish in 2021. This team is headlined by multiple top-tier players at their respective positions based on their Week 1 performance — including Murray, Gibson, Carter II, Diggs, Samuel, and Anderson. They may not be the big names, but they all brought it in Week 1, and despite the loss, this team has some legit potential to push into the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: Winning despite a negative PFAA — Rolls with Butter needs a trade to climb before Week 3.
teams.blurb: He might be one of the most hated fantasy managers of the past two years, while also being one of the most successful, but he has yet to win a PFFL championship. Rolls with Butter is my lowest-ranked team that won last week, because he has a negative PFAA (points for/against average) — meaning that he probably would've lost if he played a team that had WRs. One positive: he has the 2nd-best DR (depth rating) in the league at 35.6. Look for this manager to trade before the start of Week 3, boosting him up the ranks.

teams.synopsis: Positive PFAA despite injury losses, but a bottom-2 finish looms by next week.
teams.blurb: Quigley didn't have the best luck in Week 1 with the loss of <mark class="hl-player">Allen</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Mitchell</mark>, but not all hope is lost. He finished with a positive PFAA even with the injuries. That being said, I don't believe this team has what it takes to win Week 2, and it might drop to a bottom-2 team by this time next week.

teams.synopsis: Jalen Hurts looks the part, but a .5 boom-to-bust ratio says the stars need to show up.
teams.blurb: Led by Jalen Hurts, this team has what it takes to be an above-average squad, but the top draft picks must play better for this team to win. N.Y. Routensss had a .5 boom-to-bust ratio in Week 1, emphasizing the fact that his top guys (Deebo and Jones) must perform in the future. Look for this team to make a splash in Week 2 and jump up the ranks.

teams.synopsis: Perennial cellar-dweller status, with too much faith placed in Pierce this week.
teams.blurb: Here he is, the perennial clown of the PFFL. Geg always finds himself down here, but how long will he be down here for? One reason why his team might've failed in Week 1 is due to the amount of trust placed in <mark class="hl-player">Pierce</mark>, but if this team can make some roster moves and upgrade at certain positions, this team can see a much different placement in Week 2.

teams.synopsis: A league-worst 27.0 DR and a banged-up backfield keep The Minutemen buried for now.
teams.blurb: Is Najee's injury serious? Is Akers the RB2 in LA? Will Miles Sanders continue his comeback season? All of these questions must be answered to know how much success The Minutemen will have in 2022. With one of the worst DR's (27.0) in the league, we'll see if this team can rebound from the disappearance of Cam Akers — but it's not looking great. Don't expect this team to climb the list until Week 3 at the earliest.

teams.synopsis: Worst boom-to-bust ratio in the league, but a projected 115.2 says this was just a blip.
teams.blurb: Our final team of Week 1 rankings. Now, I don't think this team deserves to be here at all, and here's a stat to prove it: Kamara Harris had the lowest boom-to-bust ratio in the league at .33 (2 booms and 6 busts). If this trend continues in Week 2, then maybe we have to start questioning this team, but I think it was just an off week and they'll rebound next week. They're projected for 115.2 points in Week 2, which is above average, so no one should be surprised when this team shoots up the ranks into the top 8.
